#### Description

These changes should've merged in https://github.com/mitmproxy/mitmproxy/pull/6954 but somehow slipped through while restructuring functions

> Now one caveat to this method is that, sometimes we might incorrectly identify data that would not contain compression pointers like A, AAAA records to contain compression pointers since their data might have a byte with a leading 0b11. In such a case, we hope that it raises a struct.error somewhere (eg: pointer out of index, pointer points to corrupt data) in the code that is silenced by the except struct.error block. Hope this explanation clears things a bit.

Quoted from https://github.com/mitmproxy/mitmproxy/pull/6954#issuecomment-2188177515

The test example in this PR contains a "fake pointer" in the SOA record

#### Checklist

 - [x] I have updated tests where applicable.
 - [ ] I have added an entry to the CHANGELOG.
title: Fix decompressing fake pointers in DNS messages
